messages.content: Hi What can you do for me

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Hello! 👋 I’m here to help you out with almost anything you’re curious about—whether it’s quick facts, deeper explanations, creative writing, coding assistance, planning trips, learning new skills, or just having a chat. Here’s a snapshot of some things I can do: | Category | Example Tasks | |----------|---------------| | **Information & Research** | • Answer trivia or explain concepts
• Summarize news articles or research papers
• Fetch real‑time weather, stock prices, or sports scores (via web APIs)
• Look up definitions, translations, or pronunciations | | **Writing & Editing** | • Draft emails, reports, essays, poems, stories, scripts
• Proofread grammar, style, tone, and readability
• Generate outlines or bullet points from raw notes | | **Coding Help** | • Write, debug, or refactor code in many languages (Python, JavaScript, C++, etc.)
• Explain algorithms, data structures, design patterns
• Create unit tests or documentation | | **Learning & Tutoring** | • Solve math problems step‑by‑step
• Teach programming fundamentals, machine learning basics, statistics, physics, chemistry, history, literature, etc.
• Offer practice quizzes or flashcards | | **Planning & Organization** | • Build itineraries, packing lists, event schedules
• Set reminders, create checklists, manage budgets
• Suggest meal plans, grocery lists, or recipe ideas | | **Creative Projects** | • Brainstorm story plots, character arcs, worldbuilding details
• Compose music lyrics, poetry, jokes, riddles
• Design logos, UI mockups, or marketing copy | | **Technical Support** | • Troubleshoot software/hardware issues
• Configure network settings, VPNs, Docker containers
• Guide through installation steps | And much more! If you'd like me to pull fresh information from the internet—for example, current events, live data feeds, or specific websites—I can use my built‑in `requests_get` tool to retrieve JSON/XML responses directly. --- ### How would you like to start? 1. Tell me a bit about what you're working on right now. 2. Or give me a direct task/question (e.g., “Explain Newton’s second law” or “Help me write a cover letter”). Feel free to let me know your preferences, and I'll tailor my support accordingly!
